title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the continuation of La Longue Marche. There he studies profinite groups M_{φ,σ} (also written M_{ρ,σ}), built from the profinite completion of SL(2)/GL(2)-type groups and from Galois-like data. On the next page M_{ρ,σ} is described as an extension of a group T_{ρ,σ} by G^+_{ρ,σ} ≅ SG. On this page he has finished analysing M_{φ,σ} ('cf p. 495'') and returns to an auxiliary group SM_{φ,σ}.

1. Definition. SM_{φ,σ} is the semi-direct product L_0 ⋊ M_{φ,σ}. Here L_0 is a subgroup of SG, presumably procyclic or abelian of rank one, such as a Ẑ or Ẑ(1)-type unipotent or loop subgroup. M_{φ,σ} acts on L_0 through a character χ : M_{φ,σ} → Ẑ^*, presumably cyclotomic-like, by multiplication: u·λ = χ(u)λ.

2. Formula (165). There is an isomorphism ε_{L_0} : L_0 ⥲ Ker(SM_{φ,σ} → M_{φ,σ}), the canonical inclusion of the normal factor. It is induced by a previously fixed ε_0, probably a chosen generator or identification of L_0.

3. Formula (166). Conjugation by u ∈ M_{φ,σ} in SM_{φ,σ} gives u ε_{L_0}(λ) u^{-1} = ε_{L_0}(μλ), with μ = χ(u). This is just the defining action of the semi-direct product.

4. Purpose. The next page (section XXI 9°) uses SM_{ρ,σ} to construct sections and subgroups of M_{ρ,σ} over T_{ρ,σ}. It also uses it to state an isomorphism SM_{ρ,σ} ≅ Σ*_{ρ,σ}. That is, it models an arithmetic or Galois-type extension group as a semi-direct product of a twisted procyclic group by M. This is the typical way a group of the form Ẑ(1) ⋊ (Galois-like group) arises, as an analogue of an inertia or cusp stabilizer.

The page itself contains only these definitions; a heading 'Les groupes S…' is begun and struck out.
errors: No mathematical error. Formula (166) is the tautological action in a semi-direct product. It presupposes that L_0 is a Ẑ-module (abelian), so that μλ makes sense with μ ∈ Ẑ^*. That is consistent with L_0 being procyclic, but the page does not state it.

ideas.what: Semi-direct product SM = L_0 ⋊_χ M with M acting on a procyclic subgroup through a character, kernel identified via ε_{L_0}
ideas.modern_name: Semi-direct product with a twisted procyclic group (e.g. Ẑ(1) ⋊ G, Tate-twisted inertia)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory; Ẑ(1) ⋊ Gal structures standard in anabelian geometry / Ihara, Deligne, Drinfeld GT context
ideas.where_published: Analogous structures implicit in Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche discussions of Galois actions on fundamental groups; this specific group unpublished

deep.surprise_reason: A short page with a routine semi-direct-product definition and its tautological conjugation formula. It contains no new result or connection; its interest lies only within the larger unpublished development of the M_{φ,σ} groups.
transcription_corrections: 'étant [?] bien comprise' — likely 'étant ainsi bien comprise'.
(165) should read: ε_{L_0} : L_0 ⥲ Ker(SM_{φ,σ} → M_{φ,σ}) (the crossed-out symbols preceding it are a struck-out attempt, e.g. 'u_{...}').
'correspondant à ε_0, [-défini-] on aura, par construction' — the 'défini' is crossed out and replaced by 'construction'; reading otherwise correct.
The struck-out final line appears to read 'Les groupes S…' (incomplete).
